dream: The card boiled until the dark oak felt heavy. I pressed down, trusting the lean while the stall sat cool on the ground. The roof I drew caught the air, thick as wet paper. The wedge bit tiredly against the slip, which refused to move. I swapped the plant for the stall, making the ground cold. The grind spun, eating the old stump to make room for the weight. Then the wedge grew thin under the new pressure. The flat anchor lay wide, then vanished. I fell asleep inside the boiling square, a dot safe in a frame that wavered and melted.
